summary: Local credential cache corruption after Kerberos policy push prevents interactive login and SSO token refresh
description:
Issue summary:
Users report they cannot unlock laptops or authenticate to internal web apps after a Kerberos policy push that rotated the realm mapping. Affected endpoints show repeated sssd/sshd and winbind errors and the local credential cache (ccache) file appears zero-length or corrupted after a reboot.

Impact:
- Several desktop engineers in us-west cannot SSO to internal dashboards and must use recovery codes.
- Some machines drop network mounts that rely on Kerberos tickets (NFS mounts failing).
- Blocks pair-programming and local test runs for ~20 users (approx 15% of devs in region).

Environment:
- Hybrid AzureAD-joined laptops managed by Redwood Intune + an on-prem AD/ADFS/Kerberos realm (krb5).
- Affected OSes: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (custom imaging), Windows 11 22H2 (corporate image).
- Provisioning agents: corp-provisioner v3.4.1 and endpoint-sidecar v1.9.

Steps to reproduce (from one repro machine):
1) Boot a hybrid-joined Ubuntu 22.04 workstation with existing cached tickets.
2) Apply the Kerberos realm mapping change via the central config push (ansible job kerberos-realm-rotate).
3) Reboot as prompted by the policy agent.
4) Attempt to unlock screen or run klist / kinit.

Observed behavior:
- On boot, systemd services sssd.service and winbind.service fail to start transiently with exit code 203 (unit configuration problem) and then later report STATUS=failed.
- /tmp/krb5cc_* files created but show 0 bytes. klist returns "klist: Credentials cache file '/tmp/krb5cc_1000' not a valid ccache file".
- On Windows, cached Kerberos tickets are evicted and ADFS SSO redirects to a login loop; Windows Event Viewer shows Schannel warnings and LSA kerberos errors referencing 0x8009030E.

Expected behavior:
- Policy push should rotate realm mappings without corrupting on-disk ccache files; services should gracefully restart and re-acquire tickets or prompt user for interactive re-auth to recover.

Logs and artifacts collected:
- /var/log/sssd/sssd_pam.log: "[sdap] Could not open ccache file: Invalid ccache"
- journalctl excerpt: "sssd[pid]: Could not initialize ccache: Bad file descriptor"
- /var/log/syslog contains the ansible job timestamp and agent restart markers.
- Attached: anonymized klist/kinit outputs and sample zero-byte ccache metadata (sha256 sums and inode info).

Immediate mitigation attempted by reporter:
- Manual removal of zero-byte ccache files and recreation with kinit succeeds for single-user session (interactive), but corruption recurs after next policy push or reboot.
- Workaround for now: disable automated kerberos-realm rotate job for us-west while we investigate (Ops rollback implemented 2026-03-12 22:15 PDT).

Additional notes:
- Change was rolled out to all regions; only us-west has user reports so far (suspect timing/ordering with provisioner).
- Ansible job uses a templated /etc/krb5.conf replacement and signals provisioner via SIGHUP.

Recommended next steps listed below in investigation notes.
investigation_notes:
Investigation timeline:
- 2026-03-12 20:30 PDT: Ticket created by Priya after multiple Slack reports (#internal-support).
- 2026-03-12 21:00 PDT: Confirmed repro on Ubuntu image; zero-byte ccache appears immediately after policy handler restarts sssd.
- 2026-03-12 22:15 PDT: Ops rolled back kerb-rotate job to stop additional machines being affected.
- 2026-03-13 09:40 PDT: Repro attempted on Windows 11 VM image; observed LSA failure patterns similar to on-prem bug KB12345.
- Hypothesis A: Provisioning agent restarts sssd/winbind before krb5 config is fully written to disk, leaving ccache creation in a bad state (race).
- Hypothesis B: New krb5.conf template changes default ccache format/permissions and an older agent version mishandles binary ccache -> creates empty file.
- Actions taken: captured strace of sssd startup (shows EIO when opening /tmp/krb5cc_1000 after SIGHUP), compared krb5.conf diffs, verified agent version on repro machine differs from fleet by one minor patch.
- Correlation: machines with endpoint-sidecar v1.9 (and provisioner v3.4.1) consistently repro; machines with sidecar v2.0-beta do not.
- A/B test: Pinned sidecar to 2.0-beta on two repro machines -> no corruption after policy push.

Temporary risk assessment: Recurrent corruption could lead to mass-login failures if rotation resumes; severity raised to Sev2 due to partial regional impact and user productivity loss.

resolution:
Workaround/temporary resolution:
- Kerberos rotate job rolled back for us-west to prevent further surface area.
- Users can manually recreate tickets with kinit after removing zero-byte ccache files; this is a stop-gap.

Planned permanent fix:
- Provisioner team to land two changes: (1) ensure krb5.conf write is atomic + fsync before signalling agent, (2) upgrade endpoint-sidecar on repro fleet to v2.0 which avoids the empty-file bug.
- GH PR #7832 (prov/signal-ordering) and GH PR #7835 (agent version pin) linked.
- Post-change canary scheduled 2026-03-15 02:00 PDT for 20 machines in us-west; monitoring dashboard panels created (dashboards/kerberos/INT-842468-canary).

Follow-ups:
- Run full audit of machines that received the original rotate change for potential ticket replay or stale mounts (assigned to Marco).
- Update Confluence runbook with steps to recover corrupted ccache files and add agent compatibility note.

Status: In Progress - awaiting provisioner PR merge and staged canary deployment.
